subject: Implementation kickoff: traffic shaping & SDK cutover for AtlasPay
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood-inference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation kickoff: traffic shaping & SDK cutover for AtlasPay

Priya —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. I wanted to kick off the implementation thread and outline the immediate plan for SDK setup, endpoint migration, and traffic shaping controls so we can align expectations before the handoff call. Short summary and asks below: 

What we want to accomplish in the next 2 weeks:
- Sandbox SDK install and smoke test (SDK + example app)
- Endpoint migration plan (dev -> staging -> prod) with cutover window and rollback criteria
- Traffic shaping rules to protect both sides during ramp (rate limits, burst handling, prioritization)
- Telemetry and QA checks (latency/err rates, KV cache priming)

Quick asks for AtlasPay:
1) Confirm the API domain(s) you want us to call from staging and prod.
2) Send any hard token/secret rotation windows (if applicable).
3) Attach telemetry spec if you have one (sample fields we can emit).

Attachments: I uploaded a short starter kit (sdk-setup-samples.zip) and a mutual action plan template (mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

Implementation approach (high level):
1) SDK install in sandbox using our node/python packages. Example Node snippet (run in sandbox):

const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://sandbox.redwood.ai' });
async function smoke() {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', prompt: 'hello test', maxTokens: 8 });
  console.log(res.text);
}

2) Use traffic shaping: start with 10 QPS, 200ms timeout, 3 retry attempts (exponential backoff) during staging ramp.
3) Cutover: schedule a short traffic switch (5–15 min) and monitor the dashboards; rollback if error rate > 2% for 5 continuous minutes.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff tomorrow to walk through. Grace and Vivek will own the integration plan and resiliency rules. Vanessa will coordinate SSO/SCIM details if we need account provisioning. Monica will be CS lead for post-cutover validation.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya@atlaspay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: traffic shaping & SDK cutover for AtlasPay

Jordan / team —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few constraints from our side before the call:
- Domain: staging-api.atlaspay.com and api.atlaspay.com (we can provide IP allowlist next week)
- Secrets rotation: monthly, next rotation scheduled 2026-09-20 02:00 UTC — avoid major cutovers around that window
- Rate guidance: internal gateway enforces 150 QPS per client ID; we'd like Redwood to start at 5 QPS in staging and ramp by increments of 5 every 30 minutes (monitoring required)
- Telemetry: attaching the telemetry export schema (atlaspay-telemetry-spec.pdf). We emit request_id, customer_id, route, latency_ms, upstream_status, and a request_weight field you can use for traffic shaping if needed

One more thing: our platform enforces a soft per-minute burst of 2x configured QPS, and we want a graceful backoff to avoid cascading failures. Could you include a recommended retry policy that respects Retry-After headers?

I'll join tomorrow's kickoff; Liam will bring the infra lead if there are network questions.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Shah | Head of Integrations, AtlasPay

Attachments: atlaspay-telemetry-spec.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@atlaspay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: traffic shaping & SDK cutover for AtlasPay

Thanks, Priya — this is helpful. Based on your constraints we propose the following concrete plan and resiliency defaults to include in the mutual action plan: 

Staging ramp plan (automated):
- Start at 5 QPS for 30 minutes.
- If error rate < 0.5% and median latency < 350ms, increase by +5 QPS. Repeat every 30 minutes up to 50 QPS.
- If error rate rises above 1% or 95th latency > 750ms, pause ramp and revert to previous step.

Recommended retry policy (client-side):
- Idempotent calls: up to 3 retries using exponential backoff (initial 200ms, factor 2, jitter 0.1).
- Non-idempotent (writes): avoid automatic retries; instead return 409/422 to caller and surface to monitor.
- Honor 429/503 with Retry-After if present; if Retry-After > 10s, surface as alert and do not retry more than once.

Timeouts and deadlines:
- Per-request timeout: 2s for short calls, 10s for longer text-gen flows in staging.
- Circuit-breaker: open after 6 successive 5xx responses within 60s, half-open after 30s.

Sample SDK usage patterns (Node + cURL examples included in sdk-setup-samples.zip). Inline sample for token-refresh flow: 

// minimal token refresh guard
async function callWithRefresh(client, params) {
  try {
    return await client.generate(params);
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.code === 'AUTH_EXPIRED') {
      await refreshToken(); // rotate and retry once
      return await client.generate(params);
    }
    throw err;
  }
}

Operational hooks we will enable on our side:
- Prefix caching for common prompts (to reduce hot KV misses)
- Per-route metrics dashboard (we'll share log links)
- Automated rollback policy that will flip traffic back to your previous A-record for 10 minutes if overall error budget crosses 2%

Next steps before the kickoff call:
- Priya: confirm the IP allowlist window and provide the staging API TLS certificate fingerprint if you want mTLS.
- Atlas infra: provide an example request that represents your 95th percentile so we can mimic load accurately.

We will update the attached mutual-action-plan.xlsx with the ramp windows above and the rollback criteria.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor | Principal Integration PM
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@atlaspay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>

Date: 2026-09-15T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: traffic shaping & SDK cutover for AtlasPay

Priya / team — quick operational notes from infra side ahead of tomorrow's call: 

1) IP allowlist: we will need the final list by 2026-09-17 23:59 UTC to provision staging NATs.
2) Canary window: propose 2026-09-22 02:00–04:00 UTC for the first low-traffic cutover (we will not schedule around your secrets rotation).
3) Observability: we created a shared dashboard and a temporary log sink (link in the Drive). We will enable an alert to your SRE if 429s exceed 5% in a 5-minute window.

Action items assigned: 
- Vanessa: coordinate SSO/SCIM if we need to create AtlasPay service accounts.
- Monica: own the post-cutover validation checklist and run 10 smoke scenarios.
- Grace: finalize mutual-action-plan.xlsx (I updated the ramp rules).
- Jordan: share SDK bootstrap quickstart repo and the sample cURL commands in the kickoff notes.

One last technical detail on client-side backoff we recommend: combine exponential backoff with request_weight awareness. If AtlasPay sets request_weight > 1 on some paths, the SDK should decrement effective QPS accordingly (weight-aware token bucket). We will include a small helper in sdk-setup-samples.zip to do this.

Looking forward to the call — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
